can_do: Describe getting ready (I wash, I get dressed, I prepare)
Talk about morning hygiene and preparation
Complete your full morning routine description
entries.description: Complete your morning routine: je me lave (I wash), je m'habille (I get dressed), je me prépare (I get ready)
entries.title: Getting Ready - {se laver, s'habiller, se préparer}

can_do: Talk about remembering things (I remember, do you remember?)
Express having fun and enjoyment (I'm having fun)
Say you're hurrying or in a rush (I'm hurrying)
entries.description: Essential reflexive verbs: je me souviens (I remember), je m'amuse (I'm having fun), je me dépêche (I'm hurrying)
entries.title: Daily Actions - {se souvenir, s'amuser, se dépêcher}

can_do: Describe past routines (I woke up, I got dressed, I left)
Use être with all reflexive verbs in past tense
Tell stories about what you did in your daily routine
entries.description: Tell stories about your routine in the past: je me suis réveillé(e) (I woke up), elle s'est levée (she got up)
entries.title: Reflexive Verbs in Past Tense

can_do: Express mutual actions (we love each other, they see each other)
Talk about reciprocal relationships
Use reflexive pronouns for 'each other' meanings
entries.description: Express mutual actions: nous nous aimons (we love each other), ils se parlent (they talk to each other), on se voit (we see each other)
entries.title: Reciprocal Reflexives - Each Other

can_do: Give informal commands to friends and family
Tell someone to eat, speak, go, do something
Use command form with -ER and -IR verbs
entries.description: Give informal commands: Mange! (Eat!), Parle! (Speak!), Fais attention! (Be careful!)
entries.title: Commands - tu form (Informal)

can_do: Give formal or plural commands politely
Instruct groups or strangers (Eat! Speak! Listen!)
Use vous command form in professional contexts
entries.description: Give formal or plural commands: Mangez! (Eat!), Parlez! (Speak!), Écoutez! (Listen!)
entries.title: Commands - vous form (Formal/Plural)

can_do: Use irregular commands (Be!, Have!, Go!, Do!)
Say common phrases like '{Vas-y!}' (Go for it!)
Master the most frequently used command forms
entries.description: Essential irregular commands: Sois! (Be!), Aie! (Have!), Va! (Go!), Fais! (Do/Make!)
entries.title: Irregular Commands - {être, avoir, aller, faire}

can_do: Give commands with object pronouns (Give it to me!)
Use pronouns with affirmative and negative commands
Form complex commands like 'Don't do it!' or 'Look at me!'
entries.description: Give commands with objects: Donne-le-moi! (Give it to me!), Regarde-moi! (Look at me!), Ne le fais pas! (Don't do it!)
entries.title: Commands with Pronouns

can_do: Read French stories about daily routines
Understand reflexive verbs and temporal words in context
Comprehend narrative sequences and daily life descriptions
entries.description: A story about a typical day. Uses temporal words, reflexive verbs, and all this unit's vocabulary!
entries.title: Reading - {Ma Journée}

can_do: Describe daily routines with reflexive verbs
Use temporal words to sequence events
Apply commands and routine vocabulary naturally
entries.description: Complete sentences using temporal words, reflexive verbs, and commands from this unit!
entries.title: Daily Life & Actions Practice - Fill in the Blanks

can_do: Describe daily routines (I wake up, I get dressed, I go to bed)
Give commands and instructions in French
Express reciprocal actions (we love each other)
entries.description: Test everything from this unit! Temporal words, reflexive verbs (introductions, routines), commands, and reciprocal actions.
entries.title: Unit exam · Daily Life & Actions

can_do: Explain why things happen (because, since, thanks to)
Give reasons for your actions and decisions
Connect cause and effect in French
entries.description: Learn to explain reasons and causes: parce que (because), car (for), puisque (since), comme (as), grâce à (thanks to), à cause de (because of)
entries.title: Causal & Reason Words - Explaining Why

can_do: Describe precise locations (in front of, behind, between)
Give directions and explain positions
Say 'The café is in front of the park' in French
entries.description: Learn to describe where things are: devant (in front of), derrière (behind), entre (between), au-dessus (above), au-dessous (below)
entries.title: Spatial Prepositions - Position & Location

can_do: Describe distance and proximity (near, far from, next to)
Give detailed directions with spatial relations
Say 'The café is next to the park' in French
entries.description: Learn to describe distance and proximity: près de (near), loin de (far from), à côté de (next to), en face de (across from), autour de (around)
entries.title: More Spatial Relations - Distance & Proximity

can_do: Talk about completed past actions (I spoke, I ate, I studied)
Form past tense with regular -ER verbs
Begin telling stories about what you did
entries.description: Learn to talk about completed past actions with regular -ER verbs: j'ai parlé (I spoke), j'ai mangé (I ate), j'ai étudié (I studied)
entries.title: {Passé Composé} - Regular -ER Verbs (I spoke, I ate)

can_do: Use the 4 most common irregular past forms (had, was, did, saw)
Say 'I had time', 'It was good', 'I did it', 'I saw him'
Form past tense with the most frequent verbs
entries.description: Learn the 4 most common irregular past participles: avoir → eu (had), être → été (was/been), faire → fait (did/made), voir → vu (saw)
entries.title: Irregular Past Participles - Set 1 (had, was, did, saw)

can_do: Express past desires, abilities, and obligations (wanted, could, had to)
Say 'I wanted to go', 'I could come', 'I had to work'
Use irregular past forms for modal and -RE verbs
entries.description: Learn modal verbs and -RE verbs in past tense: vouloir → voulu (wanted), pouvoir → pu (could), devoir → dû (had to), dire → dit (said), prendre → pris (took)
entries.title: Irregular Past Participles - Set 2 (wanted, could, had to, said)

can_do: Describe movement in the past (I went, I came, I left)
Use être instead of avoir for motion verbs
Master DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP verb patterns
entries.description: Learn motion verbs that use '{être}' in passé composé: je suis allé (I went), je suis venu (I came), je suis parti (I left), je suis arrivé (I arrived)
entries.title: être Verbs - DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP (went, came, left)

can_do: Make past participles agree with gender and number
Understand when to add e, s, or es to past participles
Use agreement rules correctly with être verbs
entries.description: Learn agreement rules: il est allé (he went) vs elle est allée (she went - add e), ils sont allés (they went - add s) vs elles sont allées (add es)
entries.title: Past Participle Agreement with être

can_do: Choose {avoir} or {être} for the past: {j'ai mangé}, {je suis allé}.
Make the participle agree after {être}: {elle est allée}, {ils sont allés}.
entries.description: See which verbs build the past with {être}, and when the participle adds -e or -s.
entries.title: Past with {être} - Which Verbs, Which Endings

can_do: Form imparfait for any French verb (was doing, used to do)
Describe ongoing past actions and habits
Use the 'nous stem' rule to conjugate all verbs
entries.description: Learn to form imparfait for ALL verbs using the 'nous stem' rule: je parlais (I was speaking/used to speak), il faisait beau (it was nice), on allait (we used to go)
entries.title: Imparfait Formation - All Verbs (was doing, used to do)

can_do: Choose the right past tense for every situation
Tell complete stories mixing actions and descriptions
Master the most important past tense distinction in French
entries.description: Learn when to use each past tense: Passé composé for specific events (J'ai mangé - I ate), Imparfait for descriptions/habits (Il faisait beau - It was nice, Je mangeais tous les jours - I used to eat every day)
entries.title: Passé Composé vs Imparfait - The Golden Rule

can_do: Compose complete past tense narratives
Combine scene-setting, events, reasons, and locations
Tell rich, sophisticated stories in French
entries.description: Practice combining everything: passé composé, imparfait, causal words, spatial prepositions for rich storytelling
entries.title: Past Tense Composition - Building Complete Stories

can_do: Read complete French stories in the past tense
Understand mixed passé composé and imparfait narratives
Comprehend sophisticated storytelling with causal relationships
entries.description: A story in the past using passé composé, imparfait, causal words, and spatial prepositions - bringing together all of this unit
entries.title: Reading - {Une Histoire du Passé}

can_do: Compose stories with passé composé and imparfait
Use causal words to explain why things happened
Apply past tense mastery in realistic narratives
entries.description: Complete sentences using causal words, spatial prepositions, and past tenses from this unit!
entries.title: Discourse & Past Tense Practice - Fill in the Blanks

can_do: Tell complete stories in the past tense
Distinguish between passé composé and imparfait
Use discourse markers for natural storytelling
entries.description: Test everything from this unit! Causal words, spatial prepositions, passé composé, imparfait, and the critical PC vs IMP distinction for complete storytelling mastery.
entries.title: Unit exam · Discourse & Past Tense

can_do: Use special verb forms for wishes and necessities
Form the foundation for subjunctive expressions
Prepare to express complex ideas at B2 level
entries.description: Learn verb forms that appear after '{il faut que...}' and '{je veux que...}' phrases. sois (be), ait (have), aille (go), fasse (do). Essential for telling people what you want them to do!
entries.title: Forms Used After '{il faut que}' and '{je veux que}'

can_do: Use more special forms for complex expressions
Express wishes with motion and modal verbs
Complete your subjunctive verb repertoire
entries.description: More verb forms that appear after '{il faut que...}' and '{je veux que...}' phrases. vienne (come), parte (leave), puisse (can), sache (know), comprenne (understand). Essential for wishes and commands!
entries.title: More Forms for '{il faut que}' and '{je veux que}' Phrases

can_do: Express necessity and requirements (It's necessary that...)
Tell people what needs to happen
Use '{il faut que}' with subjunctive forms naturally
entries.description: Learn to tell people what needs to happen! Essential phrases for parents, friends, work. '{Il faut que tu manges}' (You need to eat), '{Il faut qu'on parte}' (We need to leave).
entries.title: {Il faut que...} - Saying What's Necessary

can_do: Express what you want others to do (I want you to...)
Use subjunctive with wish expressions
Communicate desires about other people's actions
entries.description: Say what you want OTHERS to do! '{Je veux que tu viennes}' (I want you to come), '{Je veux qu'il parte}' (I want him to leave). Essential for relationships and work.
entries.title: {Je veux que...} - Expressing Wishes

can_do: Express emotions about what others do (I'm happy that...)
Use subjunctive with emotion expressions
Communicate feelings about other people's actions
entries.description: Express how you feel about what OTHERS do! '{Je suis content que tu sois là}' (I'm happy you're here), '{J'ai peur qu'il parte}' (I'm afraid he'll leave). Real relationship language!
entries.title: {Je suis content que...} - Emotion Phrases

can_do: Express opinions diplomatically (I think that...)
Use subjunctive with negative opinions to show doubt
Sound sophisticated when sharing viewpoints
entries.description: Express opinions diplomatically! '{Je pense qu'il vient}' (I think he's coming - belief), '{Je ne pense pas qu'il vienne}' (I don't think he's coming - doubt). Sound sophisticated!
entries.title: {Je pense que...} - Opinion Phrases

can_do: Express hypothetical situations (If I were..., I would...)
Talk about daydreams and what-if scenarios
Use conditional mood naturally
entries.description: Talk about fantasies and what-ifs! '{Si j'étais riche, j'achèterais...}' (If I were rich, I'd buy...), '{Si j'avais le temps, je voyagerais}' (If I had time, I'd travel). Everyone loves daydreaming!
entries.title: {Si j'étais...} - Daydreaming & Hypotheticals

can_do: Express past regrets (If I had known...)
Talk about what you would have done differently
Use past perfect conditional naturally
entries.description: Express regrets about the past! '{Si j'avais su, je serais venu}' (If I'd known, I'd have come), '{Si j'avais étudié...}' (If I'd studied...). Universal human experience!
entries.title: {Si j'avais su...} - Past Regret Phrases

entries.description: Add depth to stories! '{J'avais déjà mangé}' (I had already eaten), '{J'étais déjà parti}' (I had already left). Show what happened FIRST in a story.
entries.title: {J'avais déjà...} - Had Already Done Phrases

can_do: Add nuance with common adverbs (really, seriously, slowly)
Modify any verb or adjective for emphasis
Sound more natural and expressive in French
entries.description: Add nuance to EVERYTHING you say! '{vraiment}' (really), '{sérieusement}' (seriously), '{lentement}' (slowly), '{rapidement}' (quickly). Make your French sound sophisticated!
entries.title: {vraiment, sérieusement...} - Common Adverbs

entries.description: Describe multitasking! '{En mangeant, je regarde la télé}' (While eating, I watch TV), '{On apprend en pratiquant}' (We learn by practicing). Natural speech patterns!
entries.title: {En mangeant...} - While Doing Phrases

entries.description: Talk about services and appointments! '{Je me fais couper les cheveux}' (I'm getting my hair cut), '{Je fais réparer ma voiture}' (I'm having my car repaired). Adult life essentials!
entries.title: {Je me fais couper...} - {Service Phrases}

entries.description: Talk about timing! '{Avant que tu partes}' (Before you leave), '{Appelle-moi avant qu'il arrive}' (Call me before he arrives). Sequence your actions!
entries.title: {Avant que...} - Before Phrases

entries.description: Explain your purpose! '{Pour que tu comprennes}' (So that you understand), '{Je t'explique pour que tu saches}' (I'm explaining so you know). Goal-oriented communication!
entries.title: {Pour que...} - So That Phrases

entries.description: Express contrasts! '{Bien que je sois fatigué}' (Although I'm tired), '{Bien qu'il fasse froid}' (Even though it's cold). Sophisticated expression!
entries.title: {Bien que...} - Although Phrases

entries.description: Express possibilities and uncertainties! '{Il est possible qu'il vienne}' (It's possible he'll come), '{Peut-être qu'il viendra}' (Maybe he'll come). Useful for planning!
entries.title: {Il est possible que...} - Possibility Phrases

can_do: Change the verb after a wish, a need or a feeling: {je veux que tu viennes}.
Keep the verb as it is after {je pense que}, and change it after {je ne pense pas que}.
entries.description: Gather the phrases that change the verb after {que}, and the ones that leave it as it is.
entries.title: Which {que} - When the Next Verb Changes

can_do: Read sophisticated French texts about dreams and ambitions
Understand subjunctive and conditional mood in context
Comprehend B2-level emotional and hypothetical expressions
entries.description: A story about dreams and ambitions using this unit's advanced expressions: wishes (je veux que...), emotions (je suis content que...), hypotheticals (si j'étais...), and more
entries.title: Reading - {Mes Rêves et Mes Espoirs}

can_do: Use B2-level expressions naturally
Apply subjunctive and conditional structures in context
Express complex ideas with sophistication
entries.description: Complete sentences using this unit's B2 level phrases: necessity, wishes, emotions, hypotheticals, and more!
entries.title: Mastery & Nuance Practice - Fill in the Blanks

can_do: Express complex ideas with subjunctive mood
Use hypothetical and conditional structures fluently
Communicate at B2 level with nuance and precision
entries.description: Test everything from this unit! Master B2 level phrases: necessity (il faut que), wishes (je veux que), emotions (je suis content que), hypotheticals (si j'étais...), regrets (si j'avais su...), and more advanced expressions.
entries.title: Unit exam · Mastery & Nuance

can_do: Say your age and ask someone's age (I'm 25 years old)
Share personal information and birthdate
Handle essential personal conversations
entries.description: Essential life skills! Learn to say your age (J'ai 25 ans), ask others' ages (Quel âge avez-vous?), and share personal information.
entries.title: Age & Personal Information

can_do: Express giving and offering (I give you, he gives me)
Talk about gifts, help, and sharing
Use one of the top 25 most common French words
entries.description: Express giving! '{Je te donne}' (I give you), '{Il me donne}' (he gives me). Essential for gifts, help, transactions, and sharing. Rank 24 in top 100 French words!
entries.title: {donner} - To Give

can_do: Put two pronouns before the verb in order: {je te le donne}.
Replace both objects of a sentence: {je donne le livre à Marie} becomes {je le lui donne}.
entries.description: Put two object pronouns in order before the verb: {je te le donne}, {je le lui donne}.
entries.title: Pronoun Order - Two Pronouns before the Verb

can_do: Talk about sleeping, working, and living
Describe your daily life and existence
Say 'I sleep 8 hours', 'I work in Paris', 'I live here'
entries.description: Three essential daily verbs: dormir (to sleep), travailler (to work), vivre (to live). Complete your ability to describe daily life and existence!
entries.title: Daily Life Essentials - Sleep, Work, Live

can_do: Express searching and finding things (I'm looking for, I found)
Talk about lost items and discoveries
Use the natural search → find sequence
entries.description: Perfect action pair! chercher (to look for) + trouver (to find). '{Je cherche mes clés}' → '{J'ai trouvé!}' Extremely practical for daily life.
entries.title: Search & Find - {chercher, trouver}

can_do: Talk about listening and watching (I listen to music, I watch TV)
Use perception verbs beyond commands
Express sensory experiences fully
entries.description: Beyond commands! Full conjugations of écouter (to listen) and regarder (to watch/look at). '{J'écoute de la musique}' (I listen to music), '{Je regarde la télé}' (I watch TV).
entries.title: Perception Verbs - {écouter, regarder}

can_do: Coordinate social situations (I'm waiting, I arrived, I'll stay)
Talk about meetings and appointments
Use essential social coordination verbs
entries.description: Essential social verbs: attendre (to wait), arriver (to arrive), rester (to stay). Perfect for appointments, meetings, and social coordination!
entries.title: Social Situations - Wait, Arrive, Stay

can_do: Give and understand directions in French
Use compass directions (north, south, east, west)
Navigate France and help tourists confidently
entries.description: Essential navigation skills! North/south/east/west, turn left/right, give directions. Perfect for traveling and helping tourists!
entries.title: Directions & Navigation

can_do: Read official French expositions and articles
Understand sophisticated cultural and social content
Comprehend real-world French publications
entries.description: Official exposition about modern France. Demonstrates your advanced reading ability with sophisticated, real-world French text using only vocabulary you've learned.
entries.title: Reading - {La France Moderne}

can_do: Use all top 100 French words in context
Apply essential daily verbs naturally
Navigate and communicate practical information
entries.description: Complete sentences using this unit's essential vocabulary: age expressions, missing top 100 verbs, and directions!
entries.title: Daily Essentials Practice - Fill in the Blanks

can_do: Use all top 100 French words fluently
Navigate France with directions and practical phrases
Understand ~85% of everyday French conversations
entries.description: Final test for this unit! Demonstrate mastery of age expressions, all missing top 100 verbs (give, sleep, work, live, search, find, listen, watch, wait, arrive, stay), directions, and practical communication. Achieve complete French foundation!
entries.title: Unit exam · Daily Essentials

units.after_text: After this unit you can introduce yourself, say who has what and join two ideas with {et} and {mais}.
units.can_do_example_fr: Je suis {name}. J’ai un chat. Je suis fatiguée, mais contente.
units.description: Master pronouns (I, you, he), être (to be), avoir (to have), articles, basic nouns, and connectors
units.name: Essential Grammar

units.after_text: After this unit you can ask simple questions, point at things and say what you want and can do.
units.can_do_example_fr: Qu’est-ce que c’est ? Je veux ça. Je peux venir.
units.description: Ask questions, use demonstratives (this/that), essential verbs (want/can/see), add descriptions with adjectives and prepositions
units.name: Asking & Describing

units.after_text: After this unit you can say where you are going and coming from, and whose things are whose.
units.can_do_example_fr: Je viens de Denver. C’est le mien.
units.description: Master motion verbs (go, come, leave), object pronouns (it/them), and possessives (mine, yours)
units.name: Movement & Possession

units.after_text: After this unit you can ask the price, say what you do and do not do, and say when and where.
units.can_do_example_fr: C’est combien ? Je ne parle pas bien.
units.description: Survival phrases, negation (I don't), time & location words, and essential daily verbs
units.name: Everyday Words

units.after_text: After this unit you can order a coffee, say what food you like and what you ate.
units.can_do_example_fr: Je voudrais un café, s’il vous plaît. J’aime le fromage.
units.description: Talk about the past (I was, I had), express preferences and opinions, order food, and add nuance with conditionals
units.name: Time & Taste

units.after_text: After this unit you can order a meal, ask for the bill and say what you need.
units.can_do_example_fr: Je prends le poulet. L’addition, s’il vous plaît. J’ai besoin de…
units.description: Advanced communication verbs (say, take, give, put, ask), progressive tenses, expressing needs, and comprehensive vocabulary
units.name: Basic Fluency

units.after_text: After this unit you can say what you know, understand, think and believe.
units.can_do_example_fr: Je sais. Je comprends. Je pense que oui.
units.description: Express understanding, thinking, and learning: comprendre (understand), savoir (know), penser (think), plus discourse markers for natural speech
units.name: Knowledge & Learning

units.after_text: After this unit you can describe your day and tell people what to do.
units.can_do_example_fr: Je me lève à sept heures. Venez !
units.description: Sequence actions in time, describe routines, introduce yourself properly: temporal words, reflexive verbs (s'appeler, se lever, se laver), and commands
units.name: Daily Life & Actions

units.after_text: After this unit you can tell someone what you did last weekend.
units.can_do_example_fr: Samedi, je suis allé au marché. Il faisait beau.
units.description: Complete storytelling mastery: causal/spatial words (parce que, près de), passé composé (j'ai mangé, je suis allé), imparfait (j'étais, il faisait), and the critical PC vs IMP distinction
units.name: Discourse & Past Tense

units.after_text: After this unit you can say what has to happen, what you hope and what you regret.
units.can_do_example_fr: Il faut que je parte. Si j’avais su…
units.can_do_short: say what you hope and regret
units.description: B2 Level Phrases! Learn special verb forms, then use them in top practical expressions: necessity (il faut que), wishes (je veux que), emotions (je suis content que), hypotheticals (si j'étais...), regrets (si j'avais su), services (je me fais couper), and more!
units.name: Mastery & Nuance

units.after_text: After this unit you can give your age, ask the way and follow directions.
units.can_do_example_fr: J’ai trente-cinq ans. Où est la gare ? Tournez à gauche.
units.description: Complete the top 100! Essential life skills: age expressions, high-frequency verbs (give, sleep, work, live, search, find, listen, watch, wait, arrive, stay), and directions. Perfect 100% top 100 coverage!
units.name: Daily Essentials
